evidence: The hunk assigns `template: escapeTemplateLiteral(line)` as the segment's whole template, not a quoted `{{ }}` splice, so a quote in a help line would render a stray backslash; the agent also notes the identity test would fail on such a line.
guidance_note: Before reusing an escaping helper, check that the call site has the context it escapes for (inside a quoted argument versus raw template body).

evidence: The hunk sets `when: bodyGate` on each line segment, and the body container also carries bodyGate; the agent checked that render.ts:764 already ANDs parent visibility into descendants.
guidance_note: When gating a container, do not restate the same predicate on children the container structurally owns; check how the render walk propagates `when` first.

evidence: Duplicate of F1: the same escapeTemplateLiteral call on raw body text, fixed once in 0fcaf2b with `template: line`.
guidance_note: Before reusing an escaping helper, check that the call site has the context it escapes for (inside a quoted argument versus raw template body).

evidence: The 'closed help widens no row' test builds the runtime without openSettingsMenu or enterEditMode, so no `(?)` cell is present; the agent added a presence assertion so the test fails if the trigger is missing.
guidance_note: When writing a test for a feature's headline criterion, assert the feature's element is present on the measured surface before asserting anything about its cost.

evidence: synthesizeGroupDecls binds `${label} ▸` / `${label} ▾`, so the doc's `label: "(?)"` example renders `(?) ▸`, not the promised `(?)`/`✕` swap; the agent confirmed this and reworded the paragraph.
guidance_note: When a doc says 'write your own like this', render the example through the sugar it uses and compare against the behaviour the doc claims it reproduces.

evidence: The hunk adds `help.trigger` as a direct child of the outer vertical container, so it is a permanent row while edit mode is on, which contradicts HelpDisclosure.trigger's 'closed help costs no row' contract; the updated snapshot showed the extra line.
guidance_note: When two call sites consume one primitive with a documented contract, check that each placement honours that contract, and read regenerated snapshots for new lines before accepting them.

evidence: F6's fix (eaf6c7b) added withTrailingCell, which recurses into the last child of any vertical container; lowerGroup's output ends in a `when`-gated body, so the trigger landed inside an unrelated group's gate. Before the fix the trigger was always visible. The agent admits 'I collapsed the two'.
guidance_note: When writing a tree-descent helper that places a node, enumerate every node shape the tree can contain, including lowered sugar like groups, and decide for each whether descending changes the placed node's visibility.

evidence: Same defect as F7 from a second scope: withTrailingCell, added by the F6 fix, descends into a group's gated body; fixed by the same 1c60e4d guard.
guidance_note: When writing a tree-descent helper that places a node, enumerate every node shape the tree can contain, including lowered sugar like groups, and decide for each whether descending changes the placed node's visibility.

evidence: The doc still said edit mode's `(?)` sits 'below the bar' after F6's fix moved it onto the last row; the agent replied 'My own change in the previous round made this stale'.
guidance_note: When a fix changes where something renders, grep the docs for prose describing that placement and update it in the same commit.

evidence: lowerGroup defaults the body to `direction: "vertical"` while declareHelp builds a horizontal body, so a multi-line group copied from the doc stacks. The 'row of plain text cells' advice was in the original PR text and was not introduced by the F5 fix.
guidance_note: When a doc tells authors to reproduce a built-in with sugar, list every default where the sugar differs from the built-in (glyphs, direction) in the same pass.

evidence: withTrailingCell shipped in eaf6c7b with only the horizontal branch exercised, and the untested vertical branch held the F7 bug. The agent added root-shape tests instead of branch tests plus a hue assertion, arguing the hue invariant holds by construction and the byte snapshots already cover it.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a helper with several branches, add a fixture that reaches each branch before pushing; here the vertical-descent fixture would have surfaced F7 in the same commit.

evidence: The hue shift is real (hue.step is 14), but nextHueShift is a pre-order leaf count, so moving leaves inside the menu subtree cannot change the index of any leaf after it; the proposed trailing move does not fix the whole-bar shift the finding argues from. The agent documented the arithmetic and kept the code.
guidance_note: When one call site deliberately departs from a discipline a sibling call site follows, write the reason at the departing site in the original PR.

evidence: The hunk changes EDIT_MODE_GATE from the literal `{{ eq .edit.mode "open" }}` to disclosureGate(...), which emits `{{ and (eq ...) }}`, while docs line 716 still quoted the old literal. This drift came from the original PR's refactor.
guidance_note: When a refactor changes generated text, grep the docs for verbatim quotes of the old output.

evidence: Leaves after a non-trailing anchor do shift, but the shift is set by the anchor's author-chosen position and the leaf count, not by where the trigger sits inside the menu, so the implied trailing fix does not apply. The agent recorded this in the f6d0542 comment.
guidance_note: When one call site deliberately departs from a discipline a sibling call site follows, write the reason at the departing site in the original PR.

evidence: After 0fcaf2b stopped escaping help lines, disclosure.ts's comment still listed 'a help line' as a use of escapeTemplateLiteral; the agent replied 'My round-one change made this stale'.
guidance_note: When a fix removes a call to a helper, read the helper's own doc comment for examples naming the removed caller.

evidence: The F12 fix comment (f6d0542) said four leaves, but PERSIST_HELP has two lines, so it adds three; the count was copied from edit-chrome. The agent removed the number instead of correcting it.
guidance_note: When a comment states a count of something defined elsewhere, check the count against its source, or describe it derivably instead of copying the number.

evidence: The F7 fix (1c60e4d) added a gated-row exception where the trigger takes its own line, while the same round's F9 doc rewording described only the trailing case; the agent replied 'My previous round introduced both halves of this'.
guidance_note: When a fix adds an exception to a documented behaviour, update the doc sentence describing that behaviour in the same push.

evidence: nextHueShift counts leaves over the whole tree, so 'after the content it explains' is not cost-free unless the help is the last leaf of root. This advice was in the original doc text, not added by a fix.
guidance_note: When writing advice derived from an invariant, state it at the invariant's real scope (the whole tree), not the scope of the doc's example.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: e8ce89b touched only the `(?)` section, while the stale ASCII menu at docs line ~937 has been stale since the PR's base commit added the settings-menu `(?)`.
guidance_note: When adding a visible element to a bundled surface, grep the docs for illustrations of that surface and update them.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: declareHelp's gateOf(within) on the trigger predates review, and e8ce89b only edited a comment. On the merits, the agent showed that help.body is a sibling of the gated row (consistent with F12's listing of the row order), so `within: []` would strand the body, and both gates already derive from one disclosureGate(SETTINGS_REF).

narrative: The round-0 blocking fix for F6 introduced withTrailingCell. It regressed visibility for group-ending roots (F7/F8), shipped without branch coverage (F11), and left doc prose stale (F9); the follow-up exception then drifted the doc again (F17). Two other fixes left comment drift: F1's escape removal left disclosure.ts naming help lines (F15), and F12's explanatory comment carried a copied, wrong leaf count (F16). Every round still contained at least one finding not caused by a fix, so no whole round was avoidable, but 7 of the 20 findings were caused by fixes. The agent's pushbacks on the settings-menu hue finding (F12/F14) and the trigger gate (F20) were sound and checked out against the arithmetic.
guidance_observations: Fixes that introduced a new helper were pushed with tests reaching only the branch the bundled default exercises; one fixture per node shape would have caught F7 in the same commit.
Each placement change was followed a round later by a doc-drift finding; a grep of the docs for the changed placement's wording before pushing would have saved those threads.
Comments written in response to findings copied facts (a leaf count) from elsewhere instead of deriving them, and the reviewer caught the copy the next round.

evidence: The e0aea25 diff shows render() never called hueStepRows or faithfulHueStep, and the HS/HO/CL sliders fed only dead functions. The agent took the reviewer's delete option, removing that machinery and rewriting the intro.
guidance_note: Before publishing a demo cited as evidence, delete every control and function the render path no longer reaches, and reread the intro against what actually renders.

evidence: The reviewer admitted it could not verify; the agent reports `Object.keys(getThemePalette(t))` is `['name','dark','vars']`, which the packet does not independently show (the later d7ac366 throw uses `${P.name}`, which is consistent). The cache was deleted in e0aea25 anyway, which makes the question moot.

The original code had DIST and MENU_STYLE as separate tables with different membership and different formulas (monotonic `(i+.5)/n` versus ramp `k/(n-1)`), contradicting the doc's 'one mechanism'. e0aea25 merged them into one DIST table.
guidance_note: When a design doc claims two surfaces share one mechanism, make the demo code literally share one table before citing it.

evidence: `open:!!node.menu` is true for an empty array, so the ≡ trigger was always open. The agent made `menu` a total field so `open` is `menu.length>0`, which also lets bands render recursively.
guidance_note: Avoid optional fields where absence and emptiness mean the same thing; make the field total so truthiness checks cannot diverge.

evidence: The inconsistency was real: decorBg guarded with a silent `surface` fallback while menuPlane did not. The agent reports all 23 themes resolve all 8 roles, so it deleted the guard instead of copying it.
guidance_note: Do not add a fallback branch for a role lookup without first checking whether the role can actually be missing; a silent substitute is worse than a throw.

evidence: The doc's table row said '42° step' while the text says leaf i gets i*14 degrees; 42 is the separation between visible neighbours. The agent reworded the row.
guidance_note: When a table reports an emergent number next to a configured one, label which is which.

evidence: The regen instructions created an untracked `./rj-entry.mjs` at the repo root. e0aea25 pipes the entry on stdin instead, so no file is left behind.
guidance_note: Run documented regeneration commands once in a clean checkout and confirm git status stays clean.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the surface-only `decorMax=mixc(S,hue,0.30)` is in the original round-0 code, and e0aea25 only removed the cache around it. The premise held: the agent measured solarized-dark/secondary at 2.15 against the surface-lighten-1 tint.
guidance_note: When a guarantee is stated over a vocabulary (every base), make the check iterate the same vocabulary constant rather than one hand-picked member.

evidence: The F4 fix in e0aea25 made the ≡ trigger switch between tint and state colour as the slider crosses 0→1, while the intro rewritten in the same commit claimed 'no existing cell changes'. Before the fix, ≡ was always open, so it never changed.
guidance_note: After changing what a slider toggles, reread the intro text that describes the slider's effect against the new behaviour before pushing.

evidence: The F3 fix (e0aea25) deleted MENU_STYLE, but the doc line measuring 'neutral-base variation' and 'alternating' survived as unchanged context in that same diff.
guidance_note: When deleting a table, grep the doc for each of its keys and remove or restate every measurement that cites them.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the original stateColor already ended with `break; ... return c` on exhaustion, and 65a4a5c only widened the loop to k<=12. The silent under-floor return predates review; d7ac366 made it throw.
guidance_note: When a loop searches for a value that must satisfy a stated floor, make exhaustion throw rather than return the last candidate.

evidence: The figures check: 360/8=45 at n=7, and stepping's minimum over d<7 of 42d's distance from a full turn is 42 (at n=10, 378→18). The sentence just never named its measure. The flag is a false positive: the sentence is original text untouched by 65a4a5c.
guidance_note: When quoting a series next to a table, name which column's measure the series uses.

evidence: The code starts the search at `mixc(surface,hue,0.92)`, which the doc never states. Both the doc wording and the 0.92 start are in the original round-0 code, so the d7ac366 flag is a false positive; the agent took the reviewer's doc option.
guidance_note: When a doc describes an algorithm as the reproducible contract, state its starting value and constants, not just its direction.

evidence: The per-item menuPlane recompute is real, but the agent measured a full render at 2.56 ms with hl=30, so the cost is negligible in a demo harness. The redundant call predates the d7ac366 flag. A per-pass memo is a derived cache, not a second source of truth, so the law citations stretch.

narrative: This is a design-doc and demo PR. Round 0 found dead comparison machinery, a split distribution table, an always-open trigger and doc imprecision, all fixed in one large rewrite (e0aea25). That rewrite caused two drift findings: the new intro's isolation claim ignored the trigger's own open toggle (F9), and a doc measurement still cited deleted MENU_STYLE variants (F10). Most ON-NAMED-FIX flags in rounds 1-3 are false positives on code that predates review (surface-only decorMax, silent loop exhaustion, the 0.92 start point, per-item menuPlane). The pushbacks (F2, F14) were reasonable, though F14's law citation was a stretch.
guidance_observations: A wholesale rewrite in answer to round-0 findings was not followed by a grep of the doc for names from the deleted tables, which left F10 for the next round.

Several later findings targeted original logic that the earlier rewrite had carried over unexamined; a fresh read of each surviving function against the doc's claims during the rewrite would have batched them into one round.
